name: MASS Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Revised Ghent Criteria for MASS Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of mitral valve prolapse confirmed by echocardiography
Aortic root dilation without progression to aneurysm
Presence of skeletal features including pectus deformity, scoliosis, or joint hypermobility
Skin striae without significant skin fragility or atrophic scarring
Family history of MASS syndrome or related connective tissue disorders

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Mitral valve prolapse and skeletal features must be present; aortic root dilation supports diagnosis but is not mandatory.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: MASS syndrome is differentiated from Marfan syndrome by absence of ectopia lentis and less severe aortic involvement.

pathognomonic.notes: Confirmed by echocardiography, hallmark cardiac feature
Generalized ligamentous laxity without severe dislocations
Stretch marks without significant skin fragility

common.notes: Chest wall deformities common in connective tissue disorders

occasional.notes: Less frequent than in Marfan syndrome

rare.notes: Rare complication due to connective tissue weakness
Extremely rare in MASS syndrome compared to Marfan syndrome
searchTerms: sudden chest or back pain from artery tear

imaging: Echocardiography showing mitral valve prolapse and aortic root measurements
Spinal X-rays demonstrating scoliosis or chest wall deformities
MRI for detection of dural ectasia
genetic: FBN1 gene mutations associated with MASS phenotype but distinct from classic Marfan syndrome mutations
other: Clinical evaluation of joint hypermobility using Beighton score

distinguishingFeatures: More severe and progressive aortic root dilation
Arterial tortuosity and aneurysms throughout the arterial tree
Aggressive vascular disease with early rupture risk

redFlags: Rapid progression of aortic root dilation
Severe mitral regurgitation causing heart failure symptoms
Sudden onset chest pain or dyspnea suggestive of aortic dissection or pneumothorax
references: Loeys BL, Dietz HC, Braverman AC, et al. The revised Ghent nosology for the Marfan syndrome. J Med Genet. 2010;47(7):476-485.

Faivre L, Collod-Beroud G, Loeys B, et al. Effect of mutation type and location on clinical outcome in 1,013 probands with Marfan syndrome or related phenotypes and FBN1 mutations: an international study. Am J Hum Genet. 2007;81(3):454-466.
MASS phenotype: clinical features and differential diagnosis. Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases. 2014.
